newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila businessmen say against Ramos re-election.
newsitem.headline: Manila businessmen say against Ramos re-election.

text.p: Two leading business groups in the Philippines said on Friday they oppose a proposed change in the constitution to enable President Fidel Ramos to contest a second term in office.

"We believe that such efforts are not advisable because they would derail the economic momentum that such moves ostensibly seek to preserve," the Makati Business Club and the Management Association of the Philippines said in a joint statement.
Ramos, who was elected to a six-year term in 1992, is prohibited from seeking re-election under the constitution. The terms of other senior elected officials are also restricted.
But a movement to amend the laws has gathered pace this week, with supporters saying that the economic boom in the country would fizzle out if Ramos were to leave office.
There is also strong opposition to the move. Ramos has said he does not wish to serve another term but has refused to sign a pledge to that effect.
The business groups said the economic reforms initiated by Ramos could be affected by any amendment of the laws.

"We credit the present administration for providing the political and business climate for a thriving economy," they said in the statement. "In order to help these changes gain greater momentum, we need to protect the stability of our institutions, of which the most basic is the constitution."
